evidence.quote: At present, it looks likely that r* will remain low for the policy-relevant future
A variety of models and statistical approaches suggest that the current level of short-run r* may be close to zero.
the Federal Reserve's normalization tools proved effective in raising the federal funds rate following our December meeting.
if asset prices across the economy--that is, taking all financial markets into account--are thought to be excessively high, raising the interest rate may be the appropriate step.
Negative policy rates have generally not been associated with the problems that likely were anticipated.

parsed.rationale: A largely academic speech on low r*, ZLB tools and financial stability. Emphasis on persistently low r* implies a lower rate path (mildly dovish), balanced by openness to leaning against asset-price excesses and satisfaction with normalization.
